newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb seed operations boost earnings.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb seed operations boost earnings.

text.p: DeKalb Genetics Corp said Wednesday gains from its domestic and international seed operations boosted earnings for fiscal 1996 to $1.03 a share, compared with $0.61 a share from continuing operations in 1995.

"Sales volume for our corn products rose 25 percent in the United States," Bruce Bickner, chairman, said in a statement. "Overall, DeKalb captured a percentage point of additional market share, and in key Corn Belt areas, our market share gains were even greater. Our seed operation in Canada also delivered excellent results."
DeKalb said fiscal 1996 North American seed earnings rose 39 percent to $30.9 million, including $3.3 million from Monsanto Co under a research collaboration agreement.
North American seed revenues rose nearly 30 percent for the year to $259.8 million from $199.9 million.
Regarding seed supplies, Bickner said this year's summer seed crop is coming in at near-targeted levels, but is still at some freeze risk.
"We expect, though, to have an adequate seed supply next spring, although good supply utilization will again be a priority," he added.
DeKalb said international seed earnings for the year rose 32 percent to $10.0 million from $7.6 million. Revenues increased 12 percent to $80.6 million from $72.1 million.

"Other factors in our earnings improvement were continued strong performance from Argentina and a return to profitability in Mexico," Bickner said. "Last year, our Mexican joint venture reported significant losses due to currency devaluation and a difficult agricultural economy and seed market."
DeKalb reported a fourth quarter loss of $0.07 a share, compared with $0.08 a year ago. Losses are typical in the fourth quarter because of the seasonal nature of the business.
DeKalb said DeKalb Swine Breeders earned $200,000 for the year, compared with an operating loss of $900,000 a year ago. Revenues in fiscal 1996 were about flat at $47.1 million.
"Although market hog prices rebounded in 1996, feed costs were significantly higher," Bickner said.

He said breeding stock revenues and sales both declined by 21 percent from last year. "We would expect the industry to remain under pressure until we see additional relief from high corn and soybean meal prices," Bickner said.
